source.title_on_document: The Rise of Large Language Models and the Direction and Impact of US Federal Research Funding

supplement.where: Supporting Information (SI Appendix), PDF pp. 15-97 of the arXiv file
supplement.holds: Regression model (S1.2); Tables S1-S4 with alpha coefficients on semantic distinctiveness, investigator-clustered standard errors, N and R2 (pp. 80-83); within-investigator topical-distance outcome (S2.17, p. 24; Fig. S50, p. 75), with coefficients and confidence intervals plotted but no exact estimates or analysis N printed; robustness analyses including standardized predictors (Table S13, p. 92).

paper_design_summary: Observational study of US federal grant abstracts: confidential NSF (D1) and NIH (D2) proposal submissions from two R1 universities and public NSF (D3) and NIH (D4) awards, 2021-2025 (pp. 12-13). The authors detect LLM involvement as alpha and use proposal-PI-field-year regressions to relate it to semantic distinctiveness relative to the same agency's prior-year funded abstracts, with start-year, field and investigator fixed effects and funding controls; the private datasets also measure topical distance from each investigator's own prior proposals (p. 5; SI S1.2, pp. 16-17; SI S2.17, p. 24; SI S2.19, p. 25). No people were assigned to AI, and the reported associations are conditional correlations; proposal success and publication counts are outside the creativity outcomes recorded here (p. 5).

participants.who: Corpus: NSF proposal abstracts (funded, unfunded, pending) submitted by investigators at two large US R1 universities, request start dates 2021-2025; 'D1 contains 1.6K NSF proposal submissions' (p. 12). Distinctiveness analysis uses start years 2023-2025 (p. 5). Number of investigators not stated.

ai_tool.name_model: Not named for the investigators' own use; LLM involvement detected against a reference built with GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 rewrites (p. 3; SI S1.1, p. 15)
ai_tool.how_used: Self-chosen LLM use in writing proposal abstracts, measured after the fact as alpha, the estimated fraction of LLM-modified sentences (0 to 1)

task.description: Writing research proposal abstracts for NSF

outcomes.name: Semantic distinctiveness (prior 1 year), within-year percentile
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean cosine distance from the abstract's SPECTER2 embedding to all abstracts funded by the same agency in the preceding year, converted to within-year percentiles (0-100; higher means more distinctive); analysis covers grant starts in 2023-2025 (p. 5; SI S1.2, pp. 16-17). The output unit is a proposal-PI-field-year regression row: n_units = 1886 is the Model 3 observation count, not a count of distinct abstracts or people; a proposal or award may contribute multiple rows. The unique-abstract count for this analysis sample is not stated (SI S2.19, p. 25; Table S1, p. 80). Robustness variants: prior-two-year reference window (SI S2.5, p. 19; Fig. S8, p. 33); L2 distances and raw cosine distances without percentile normalization (SI S2.6, p. 19; Figs. S9-S10, pp. 34-35); alternative reference LLMs Claude, Gemini and Llama (SI S2.10, pp. 20-21; Fig. S27, p. 52), with Gemini-based distinctiveness results explicitly not statistically significant; tokenization, stopword and punctuation variants (SI S2.11, pp. 21-22; Fig. S31, p. 56); AI-vocabulary exclusion (SI S2.12, pp. 22-23; Fig. S35, p. 60); minimum abstract lengths of 100, 150 and 250 words (SI S2.14, pp. 23-24; Fig. S40, p. 65); a single-/multi-investigator indicator control (SI S2.15, p. 24; Fig. S44, p. 69); predictors standardized to z-scores while the outcome remains a percentile (SI S2.16, p. 24; Fig. S47, p. 72; Table S13, p. 92); and one field per proposal or award (SI S2.19, p. 25; Fig. S52, p. 77). Stylistic-rewriting calibration of baseline abstracts found nearly indistinguishable average distinctiveness for original and rewritten text; this comparison does not assign people to AI (SI S2.1, p. 17; Fig. S1, p. 26).

contrasts.reported: Table S1, alpha: Model 1 -16.456*** (4.455), N = 1001; Model 2 (start year + field FE) -11.2727** (3.9927), N = 1412; Model 3 (start year + field + investigator FE) -11.9472** (4.3752), N = 1886, R2 = 0.72441. Controls log(funding). Standard errors clustered by investigator in parentheses; * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001.

outcomes.name: Within-investigator topical distance (own proposals in the previous two years)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine distance between each NSF proposal submitted in 2023-2025 and the investigator's own proposals submitted within the previous two years to the same agency; this measures departure from the investigator's recent proposal history (SI S2.17, p. 24; Fig. S50a, p. 75). Regressions include investigator, proposal-year and field fixed effects and control for proposal funding amount; standard errors are clustered by investigator. The paper defines its general regression unit as proposal-PI-field-year (SI S2.19, p. 25), but gives no analysis N or unique-proposal count for this outcome.

contrasts.reported: For private NSF proposals, the association between LLM involvement and within-investigator cosine distance is statistically indistinguishable from zero (SI S2.17). Figure S50a plots the coefficient and an investigator-clustered 95% confidence interval, but prints no exact coefficient, standard error, interval endpoints or N; no values are estimated from the plot.

eligibility.reason: All four datasets are observational: existing NSF and NIH proposal/award abstracts are compared across detected LLM involvement, with no random assignment of people to AI (pp. 5, 12-13). The number of people analyzed is not stated; regression Ns count proposal-PI-field-year observations and cannot establish the 50-person threshold (SI S2.19, p. 25; Tables S1-S4, pp. 80-83). The output-scored criterion is met by abstract semantic distinctiveness and, in the private datasets, within-investigator topical distance (p. 5; SI S2.17, p. 24; Fig. S50, p. 75). These are coded as novelty of an individual output relative to prior work; the paper explicitly describes conditional correlations, not causal estimates (p. 5), and stays outside the core dataset.

one_line_finding: In all four grant datasets, abstracts with more detected LLM text are less semantically distinct from the agency's prior-year funded abstracts, with investigator-fixed-effects coefficients on alpha of -11.9472 (private NSF), -23.3958 (private NIH), -18.0163 (public NSF), and -23.6247 (public NIH) percentile points (SI Tables S1-S4, pp. 80-83), about a 5-point drop for NSF awards and 4 points for NIH awards from the 25th to the 75th percentile of LLM involvement (p. 5).
notes: The de-identified data needed to reproduce the main plots and statistical analyses are available at the recorded data URL; raw university proposal data require data use agreements and raw Dimensions data require access from Digital Science. No separate code URL is stated (p. 14, Data and code availability).
